transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?
I’m here because I can’t get rid of this feeling that work isn’t safe anymore. And I keep thinking I’m somehow damaged now—like the competent person who got promoted isn’t really me anymore.
Can you tell me if there was a specific event or incident at work that started these feelings?
I’m not sure there was one specific incident. It feels more like work gradually stopped feeling safe, and I can’t really point to a single thing that started it.
How long have you been feeling this way about work and about yourself?
It’s been since the break-in during that overnight deployment—about two years and four months now.
Since the break-in, have you had moments where you suddenly re-experience it—like intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about that night?

Yes. A badge scanner beeping, heavy footsteps in the hallway, or a late-night deployment alert can suddenly put me right back in that office. My chest gets tight, and I see the guard on the floor even when I’m trying to focus on something else.
Aside from those flashback moments, do you also notice times when you feel detached from yourself or like things around you aren't quite real, even when nothing has reminded you of the break-in?
I don’t think so. When I’m not being reminded of it, things generally feel real and I feel like myself.
